reviews.one_line_contribution: Manipulate the fraction p of replay-verified wrong-procedure items in an ALFWorld experience bank and run six ways of consuming the same bank on the same (game, seed) cells, to ask where in each route the items get combined: whether a minority of wrong items is outvoted (aggregation) or followed (compliance) by top-k retrieval, fixed exemplars and a whole-bank long context, versus an LLM- or rule-compiled playbook that aggregates before the agent sees anything, with the claim that the static route's first advantage over retrieval is robustness rather than accuracy.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Verified by `s2cli.py paper` (S2 channel): (1) 2607.10608 'The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory' (2026-07-12) already establishes the headline behaviour — agents adopt conflicting retrieved memory at the first exposed decision point, errors compound, recovery is weak. The proposal's P2 is that result at one dose on one route; what remains is dose-response plus three extra routes, i.e. more conditions on a published effect. (2) 2608.05563 'When Experience Becomes Instruction: Trajectory Poisoning in Self-Evolving Agent Skill Systems' (2026-08-06, verified) is closer to P3/P5 than the proposal concedes: it poisons trajectories and studies whether the poison is promoted into a skill/instruction, naming 'evidence promotion' as the boundary — that is the compiled route's question, differing in outcome measure (attack success, not task success) and in lacking a matched retrieval/whole-bank comparison. (3) 2405.15556 'Certifiably Robust RAG against Retrieval Corruption' (verified, S2, 161 citations) already instantiates isolate-then-aggregate as a certified in-context defence against a bounded number of corrupted passages, which undercuts the Related Work sentence that no in-context analogue of aggregation-as-certified-defence exists; the agentic, task-success version is still open, but the framing overstates the gap. Also verified and uncited: 2608.20202 MemTrapBench (2026-08-20), which shows even faithfully recorded, relevant memories degrade current-task performance and proposes an inference-time trap-avoidance instruction. Novelty survives — none of these does a matched compiled-vs-retrieved-vs-whole-bank comparison with a dosed contamination scored on task success — but it is the narrow novelty of a factorial extension, not of a new phenomenon.
reviews.strongest_objection: The most likely interleaving of results decides the title question by construction on one side and by a pretraining prior on the other, so nothing about aggregation is learned. (a) P1 is close to entailed by this node's own Measurement A: the k=3 gain on heat/cool/clean (+39 to +55) is attributed there to the type's procedure and unseen ≈ seen, so replacing every procedure item with a goal-ineffective one must remove most of it. (b) P2, P4 and P6a are three measurements of the single fact 2607.10608 already reported; confirming all three yields 'reading routes comply', not a route contrast. (c) R3's dose-response is, in the proposal's own words, 'by construction and is reported, not predicted' — majority extraction flips at 1/2 by definition. (d) That leaves R2 as the only genuinely open cell, and its most probable outcome is the escape hatch the proposal itself names: Qwen3-32B knows ALFWorld 'heat' means the microwave, so the playbook stays clean at p=1/3 and probably at p=2/3 because the compiler overrode the sample from pretraining, not because it aggregated. The design cannot separate 'aggregates before the agent sees anything' from 'ignores the bank and writes what it already knew' — a prompt-level ban on outside knowledge is not a control and the audit is explicitly descriptive. Pre-committing to score that as P3b-falsified is honest but does not rescue the paper: the abstract's three-way contrast then collapses to 'wrong memory hurts every route that reads it, and a compiler is safe because it does not read very hard', on one environment with six templates and one backbone. Secondary but concrete, and the entailment check is right about both: P6b compares R5_j1 with R1_p1/3 in raw levels when this program has already measured k3 − static3 = +17.2 [11.9, 22.4] on a clean bank, so a ≥12-point difference is delivered by the pre-existing route gap and the claimed equivalence is excluded before any poison is added — which also violates the round's binding rule that retrieval-minus-static claims be stated against the measured +17.2. And P4, the arm the abstract says 'decides whether an in-context reader is an aggregator or a complier', sets its margin (12) equal to the stated per-cell floor (±12) on a two-seed ~137-game cell, so confirming and falsifying outcomes are not separable at the stated power.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Neutralise the compiler prior so aggregation is the only route to a correct artifact: promote the exploratory name-swap wrapper (microwave <-> stoveburner, better a fully permuted action/receptacle vocabulary across all six templates) from an exploratory R1 cell to the primary manipulation for R2/R3/R4, so the correct procedure is arbitrary and unrecoverable from pretraining. A playbook that stays correct at p=1/3 and flips at p=2/3 is then evidence about aggregation rather than about what Qwen3-32B already knows about kitchens, and P3b stops being a prediction whose falsification is the likeliest outcome. Add the dose-matched dilution control named below. Restate P6b as a difference-in-differences, (R5_j1 − R5_j0) versus (R1_p1/3 − R1_p0), so the clean-bank route gap cancels. Run R4_p0 and R4_p1/3 at 4 seeds or on the full 274-game cell so P4's floor falls below its 12-point margin, or raise that margin to 20 as in P1. Pre-register P7's slope inside the type-agnostic routes (R2/R3/R4), or as a p x route interaction, instead of pooling over routes whose pick-type context structurally cannot contain poison. Cost: the wrapper is a rename of observation/action strings and adds no episodes; the P4 and P6b fixes are about four extra cells, which the pre-registered cut order can absorb inside the ~18.5 h budget.
reviews.missing_baseline: A dose-matched uninformative (dilution) control: at each p, replace the same fraction of items with clean but procedurally useless ones — wrong-type expert trajectories, i.e. the `blind1` placebo already run in Measurement C, or items with the procedure step deleted rather than replaced. Without it every reported loss confounds 'the reader complied with a wrong procedure' with 'the reader saw two correct exemplars instead of three'. That is not hypothetical here: the node's k-sweep gives k=1 0.739/0.776 against k=3 0.807/0.869, so losing one of three correct procedure exemplars is worth several points before any compliance, and P2's 12-point margin is only ~1.4 floors. The same control is what makes P4 interpretable, since the whole-bank arm at p=1/3 loses ~13 correct procedure items as well as gaining ~13 wrong ones. Second omission, less fatal: a conflict-aware read-time route — retrieve k=3 and instruct the reader to reconcile or vote across the retrieved items, or the isolate-then-aggregate construction of 2405.15556, or an AdaptiveMem-style trap-avoidance instruction (2608.20202). Every retrieval arm here is naive consumption, so the headline that the static route's advantage is robustness is established against a version of retrieval that nobody defending retrieval would deploy on a contaminated bank.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. Queries run, all through the s2cli.py S2+HF channel (WebSearch unavailable in this session; WebFetch not used): (1) 'contamination rate of agent experience memory dose response task success compiled playbook vs retrieval' --recent -> 2607.10608, 2512.16962, 2605.13880 Preping, 2608.05784, 2607.13157, 2605.12493; nothing doses contamination across consumption routes. (2) 'poisoned experience bank fraction wrong trajectories summarized into skill library aggregation robustness ALFWorld' --recent -> 2608.11888 'Agent Skills Can Be Harmful' (2026-08-12, skill-induced failure attribution; adjacent and uncited), 2608.03509 SkillJack, 2606.15242, 2606.02540 — attacks and taxonomies, no dose-response on task success. (3) 'summarized compiled memory more robust than raw retrieved exemplars noisy incorrect memory entries agent task success comparison' --recent -> 2607.10608, 2603.02473, 2606.24775, 2607.17621; the exact comparison is absent, which supports the proposal's gap claim. (4) closest named method, 'Compliance Trap ... conflicting memory' -> 2607.10608, verified. (5) home vocabulary, no agent/memory/benchmark words, 'fraction of incorrect demonstrations in-context learning threshold majority noisy exemplars' -> 2605.26350 'When Correct Demonstrations Hurt: Rethinking the Role of Exemplars in ICL' (2026-05-25), 2411.19581 'In-Context Learning with Noisy Labels', 2601.07226 NoisyBench — none cited, and the first two are ICL-side priors the proposal should be arguing against alongside 2202.12837. (6) 'certifiably robust RAG against retrieval corruption isolate then aggregate' -> 2405.15556 RobustRAG (verified, 161 cit), 2402.07867 PoisonedRAG, 2501.00879 TrustRAG, 2410.07176 Astute RAG. Verification: I confirmed by `s2cli.py paper` every ID the novelty argument leans on — 2607.10608, 2512.16962, 2608.05563, 2601.05504, 2510.02373, 2603.21520, 2202.12837, 2303.03592, 2302.02300, 2605.24117, 2608.20202 — all eleven exist with the titles and content claimed; none failed to verify. Judging the proposal's own check: above this round's average — three query classes with IDs, a genuine home-vocabulary query with no agent/memory words, and two abstracts re-verified by ID — but with one hole and one gap. The hole: it never searched the RAG corruption-ratio and certified-aggregation literature, so the Related Work assertion that aggregation-as-certified-defence has no in-context analogue is stated without having looked, and 2405.15556 is a partial counterexample. The gap: it reports that AgentPoison was not returned by Q6 and then does not verify it by ID, leaving the single closest named attack unchecked, and the same applies to PoisonedRAG-style poison-ratio ablations, which are the dose-response prior in the adjacent field. Neither overturns novelty, but the 'no pre-emption' verdict rests on searches aimed at agent-memory security rather than at the corruption-dose literature this design actually borrows from.
